title: Career Roadmap: Data Scientist
summary: A Data Scientist uses mathematics, statistics, programming, machine learning and domain knowledge to extract insights from data, develop predictive models and support evidence-based decisions.

facts.Current degree: Integrated / Dual-Degree Programmes – IISER / NISER Integrated BS-MS (Physics / Chemistry / Biology / Mathematics / Earth Sciences)

blocks.text: A Data Scientist uses mathematics, statistics, programming, machine learning and domain knowledge to extract insights from data, develop predictive models and support evidence-based decisions.

Graduates from IISER and NISER-style integrated science programmes can enter data science by combining strong scientific reasoning with practical computing, statistical analysis and machine learning skills. Their scientific specialisation can become a competitive advantage in research-driven and domain-specific data science roles.

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Transform complex data into reliable insights, predictive models and reproducible analytical solutions to real-world problems.
Major responsibilities

items.text: Collect, clean and validate structured and unstructured data.
Explore datasets and identify patterns, trends and anomalies.
Apply statistical methods and experimental design.
Develop and evaluate machine learning models.
Translate business or scientific questions into measurable analytical tasks.
Collaborate with engineers, researchers and domain experts.
Monitor model performance and data quality.
Document assumptions, limitations and analytical conclusions.

Some graduates may enter through data analyst or research assistant positions before transitioning to Data Scientist roles. Research-intensive positions may prefer or require a PhD, depending on the employer and the complexity of the work.
The following roadmap assumes a five-year integrated BS-MS programme. The actual programme structure and elective availability differ by institution and discipline.

blocks.text: A strong portfolio should demonstrate scientific reasoning, not just the use of algorithms.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Statistical Analysis of a Scientific Dataset

Select an open dataset from physics, biology, chemistry or environmental science. Perform data cleaning, exploratory analysis, uncertainty assessment and hypothesis testing. Explain assumptions and limitations.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Predictive Machine Learning Model
Build a regression or classification model. Compare a simple baseline with at least two alternatives, use appropriate validation and analyse model errors.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Domain-Specific Science Analytics

Examples include astronomical object classification, molecular property prediction, biodiversity analysis, disease-data exploration or climate trend analysis. Select a project aligned with the core degree and available data.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: End-to-End Data Science Application
Create a reproducible pipeline for data ingestion, cleaning, model training and evaluation. Add a simple interface or API and document how the model should be used and monitored.

For each project, include the research question, dataset source, methodology, baseline, evaluation metrics, limitations and reproducibility instructions. Never claim that a model is scientifically validated solely because it achieves a high score on one test split.
For students in integrated science programmes, research internships can be especially valuable because they combine scientific depth with analytical practice.
Suitable opportunities:

items.text: Data science teams in technology companies.
Scientific software and research computing teams.

blocks.text: Useful internship responsibilities:
Maintain a project logbook and obtain permission before publishing data, code or research results from a laboratory.
Certifications can structure learning, but employers will generally also look for analytical reasoning, coding ability and project quality.
Potential learning areas:

Students may explore relevant courses from recognised universities, established online education providers and cloud training platforms. Choose courses that include practical assignments rather than relying on certificates alone.

Assist with model development and validation

Assist with modelling, experiments and scientific reporting

blocks.text: Some research-intensive, specialised or senior roles require postgraduate research experience or a PhD. Entry-level requirements vary by employer.
An integrated BS-MS can provide a strong scientific foundation. The next step should depend on the intended role rather than a default assumption that another degree is always necessary.
Potential options include:

items.text: PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science or an applied scientific discipline.
Research programmes in computational biology, bioinformatics or scientific computing.
Specialisation in machine learning or artificial intelligence.
Computational physics, chemistry or materials science.
Climate science, geoinformatics or environmental data science.
Quantitative finance, subject to the required mathematical preparation.
Industry-oriented training in cloud platforms, data engineering and ML systems.

blocks.text: For applied Data Scientist roles, a strong portfolio and relevant internships may be sufficient for some entry-level openings. Research Scientist positions often have higher academic requirements.

rows.text: Data Analyst, Research Data Analyst, Junior Data Scientist

blocks.text: Progress depends on technical depth, domain expertise, research contributions, communication, business impact and employer expectations. Research leadership may require a PhD or equivalent evidence of research capability.

blocks.text: Final Graduate Profile

A job-ready Data Scientist from an integrated science programme should combine strong quantitative reasoning, Python and SQL proficiency, statistical judgement, machine learning knowledge, scientific domain expertise and reproducible research practices.

The most effective route is to build computational skills alongside the core BS-MS curriculum, gain research or industry experience, and develop projects that solve genuine scientific or practical problems. This combination can open pathways into applied data science, scientific computing, machine learning research and specialised analytics.
